rv.q: Proof remains a scintillating play with effortless portrayals from most of the cast.
Auburn's ironclad script alone remains exceedingly enjoyable, especially for lucky newbies who don't know the bombshell that's coming.
A few technical missteps are nonetheless minor compared with the serious performance troubles at the heart of Kail's Proof.
It gets where it needs to go; what it lacks, at least for now, is elegance.

Still, the father-daughter pair does, at least, perform charmingly together. Cheadle and Edebiri are both down-to-earth and unshowy in their clear affection for each other, and they’re warmly believable as parent and child. Cheadle is laid back to the point of liquidity; he’s the only star I’ve ever...
And so will everyone else who comes to see this stunning revival.
Broadway just got smarter and deeper thanks to the return of David Auburn's Proof, a complex, curvy, and thoroughly compelling play.
The cast assembled here is easily one of the best on Broadway right now.
Proof's effective performances from its four-member cast will keep theatergoers engrossed in all of its mathematical complexities and human eccentricities until the very end.
